article.headline: Games To Watch: South Pontotoc, Booneville and Brookhaven defend unbeaten starts
article.html:
South Pontotoc’s unbeaten girls face a winning Mooreville team in New Albany, Booneville’s girls put their perfect start on the line against Starkville, and Brookhaven’s unbeaten boys visit a Lawrence County team with six wins. Those are three of the strongest record-based matchups left on Mississippi’s Tuesday varsity schedule.

This November 24, 2026, selection covers upcoming basketball and soccer, with all times Central Standard Time. The entering records below are those reported on the verified matchup pages. Earlier games are excluded; this is a selection of games to follow rather than a complete statewide schedule.

South Pontotoc’s perfect start meets Mooreville in New Albany

South Pontotoc’s girls arrive at the 4:30 p.m. meeting with Mooreville at 7–0, fresh from Monday’s 63–31 victory over Shannon. Mooreville is 5–3. The New Albany Thanksgiving Tournament matchup gives the Cougars an immediate test against a team with a winning record, with their loss-free opening on the line.

The schools’ boys teams meet at 5:45 p.m. in the same tournament. Mooreville enters 5–3 and South Pontotoc 4–3. The Cougars are trying to respond to Monday’s 48–41 loss to Alcorn Central, making this a chance to turn a close defeat into a stronger next outing against another winning opponent. Both games are listed as neutral-site fixtures, so the tournament setting matters when planning a trip.

Booneville’s girls face a strong Starkville test

Booneville’s girls host Starkville at 7:30 p.m. with a 3–0 record. Starkville brings a 5–1 mark, giving the Blue Devils an opponent with only one reported loss. Booneville beat Center Hill 58–25 on Monday; Tuesday’s meeting offers a different measure of that early form against a team that has already put together several wins.

Our Monday varsity recap has more on Booneville’s victories and the contrasting results for South Pontotoc’s teams.

Brookhaven takes its unbeaten boys record to Lawrence County

The 8:30 p.m. boys game in Monticello pairs Brookhaven at 6–0 with Lawrence County at 6–2. Both have already recorded six victories, giving Brookhaven a winning opponent as it tries to stay perfect. Brookhaven is protecting a perfect opening on the road, while the Cougars can add a victory over a team that has yet to lose. The matchup is listed as nonconference.

Kossuth hosts a basketball doubleheader with McNairy Central

Kossuth’s girls are 3–2 ahead of the 6 p.m. game against McNairy Central, which enters 3–0. The Aggies have a winning record to build on, but the visitors have not yet taken a reported loss. That contrast gives the opening game a clear question: can Kossuth stop McNairy’s perfect start on its home floor?

The boys game follows at 7 p.m., with both teams listed at 2–1. The matching records give this half of the doubleheader a different balance: each side has won more than it has lost, and each can use the nonconference meeting to build on that start.

Hancock and East Union girls try to keep perfect starts intact

Hancock’s girls are 7–0 after Monday’s 50–41 victory over Tupelo. They host Northeast Jones at 6 p.m. in Kiln. The Tigers enter 4–4, so they can move above an even record by handing the Hawks their first defeat. Hancock, meanwhile, has a quick opportunity to follow its win over the Golden Wave with another home result.

East Union’s girls carry a 5–0 record into the 6:45 p.m. trip to Belmont. The Cardinals are 2–3. The Urchins are trying to preserve their unbeaten opening away from home, while Belmont can balance its wins and losses by beating a team that has won every reported game so far.

Oxford looks to respond; DeSoto Central meets Independence

Oxford’s girls host Bayou Academy at 5 p.m. in the Charger Invitational. The Chargers are 6–1 after Monday’s 43–35 loss to Jackson Prep; Bayou is 3–6. Oxford’s first reported defeat makes this a response game, with a chance to resume the winning form that marked its opening rather than let a tournament setback carry into another day.

DeSoto Central’s boys meet Independence at 4:30 p.m. in the Senatobia Classic at Senatobia High School. The Jaguars enter 3–2 and the Wildcats 4–4. It is a neutral-site nonconference matchup: DeSoto Central can strengthen a winning record, while Independence can move above an even mark.

Gulfport and Potts Camp boys carry unbeaten records into the evening

Gulfport is 4–0 ahead of its 7:30 p.m. visit to Wayne County in Waynesboro. The War Eagles are 1–3. The Admirals have a perfect start to protect on the road, while Wayne County has an opportunity to improve its opening record against an unbeaten opponent.

Potts Camp brings a 6–0 record to the 8:45 p.m. game against Falkner at the Hickory Flat Thanksgiving Tournament. The Cardinals beat East Union 79–53 on Monday; Falkner is 0–5. The records put Potts Camp in the position of defending its unbeaten start, while the Eagles are still seeking their first reported win. This is another neutral-site tournament fixture.

Shannon’s soccer teams both bring unbeaten openings

Shannon hosts West Point at 5:30 p.m. in girls soccer. The Red Raiders enter 2–0 and the Green Wave 1–2. Shannon has won its reported matches so far, while West Point can draw level in wins and losses in the nonconference meeting.

The boys match is scheduled for 7 p.m.. Shannon is also 2–0 in that division, while West Point is 0–1–2. The Green Wave have two draws but are still seeking a first reported victory, providing a different challenge from the girls fixture as both Shannon teams try to extend winning starts.
